No, downvotes are vital. Without downvotes, you see something with a low score and you don't know if it's disliked or overlooked. Similarly, you see something with a high score and you don't know if it's got a fair number of supporters, or a lot of supporters but also some opponents.

Which I think it is how it should be. I think it would be best if every comment was treated equal. That way it is up to the reader to decide if the content is worth upvoting rather than upvoting/downvoting simply because it has already been downvoted. I think it would help with the "hivemind", which is a big turn-off of Reddit.

I completely disagree. The whole point of votes is to generate visible, unequal reactions to posts that let users estimate some combination of their quality and the standards of the community. For the kind of equality you describe, best to have no voting at all. Assuming voting, however, without downvotes you don't have a way to say "look out, I didn't like this post, you may not either." It's an advantage for spammers, low-effort posters, etc.

Don't assume downvotes are thoughtless, or if you do, don't assume upvotes are any less thoughtless. There's nothing wrong with downvotes.
